questions.explanation: The relevant evidence is the thesis itself, stated carefully. Deontology holds that duty and the right constrain the pursuit of good outcomes. This is the position defended by Immanuel Kant. The claim that deontology holds that only outcomes matter morally is a common mistake about the view, often described as "consequentialist misreading of deontology". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: rigidity in hard cases. Keeping the thesis and this mistake distinct is the point of the item.
questions.hint: Identify the consideration that makes deontology attractive.
